maya: noticing a regression on the 2x1024 longcontext job — something weird in kernel handoff tonight. FlashAttention falls back, then FFN picks cuBLASLt and we spike workspace and hit OOM on worker-8.

sven: ugh. any timeline / trace id?

maya: trace: https://internal/trace/2175/longctx-alloc-1 — short summary: seq=1024, batch=2, head_dim=128, model hidden=768. profiler shows kernel chooser -> flash fallback -> cublaslt matmul workspace ~600MB for FFN conv, peak mem jump ~800MB.

raj: can you paste the small profiler snippet?

maya: sure — pulled from the runtime trace: ```
KERNEL_CHOICE: flash_attn (attempt)
FLASH_FAIL: Triton kernel launch failed (blockDim too large) -> fallback
FFN_KERNEL: cublasLt_gemm (workspace: 614_400_000 bytes)
PEAK_DELTA: +812_000_000 bytes over baseline
OOM: gpu0 worker-8 at 2175123458
```

emily: that workspace number is the problem. cublasLt reports workspace that scales with M/K blocking; for some shapes it wants a big temp buffer. we should never let a single request trigger that without checking budget. :eyes: 

raj: agreed. two ideas: 1) runtime-side micro-probe: run a tiny probe (batch=1, same seq/head) to trigger kernel selection and read reported workspace requirement before accepting the full request. 2) maintain a fingerprint->kernel map with observed workspace sizes to avoid reprobing every time.

maya: i like probe+cache. probe should be cheap and async. if probe reports ws > soft_budget, force lower-work kernel or split request.

emily: define soft_budget: free_gpu_memory - slop. slop = max(32MB, 5% of free). also add absolute cap for cublasLt workspace per-worker (e.g. 400MB).

raj: pseudocode i sketched: ```
key = f"{seq}:{batch}:{head_dim}"
if key in ws_cache:
  ws = ws_cache[key]
else:
  ws = run_probe(shape=(1, seq, head_dim))  # triggers kernel select and returns workspace
  ws_cache[key] = ws  # ttl 10m, lru
if ws <= free - slop and ws <= per_worker_cap:
  select_kernel(best_perf_kernel_for(key))
else:
  select_kernel(low_ws_kernel)  # e.g., alternate triton/cuBLASLt fallback or split
```

maya: also need to consider KV cache pinned memory impact. prefix caching + kv buffers are sticky and reduce available free; probe should reserve kv_delta estimate when computing free.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu0 worker-8 OOM detected (2175123458) — triggered by request id longctx-1 — see /alerts/2175/oom-8

emily: telemetry: tag probe results with metric names: kernel_probe_ws_bytes, kernel_chosen, probe_latency_ms, ws_cache_hit. we can use this to tune the per_worker_cap.

maya: implementation plan: 1) add probe path to kernel chooser (opt-in flag) 2) ws_cache with small ttl + lru + eviction 3) soft_budget calc including KV overhead 4) telemetry + fallback policies. i'll open a PR.

sven: please include a unit test that simulates cublasLt requiring large workspace and validates chooser picks low-ws kernel and no OOM.

maya: will do. PR soon, will link tests and a small benchmark. :thumbsup:

raj: one more corner: quantized kernels can change workspace drastically. fingerprint should include quantization mode.

maya: good call, adding qmode to key. thanks all.

sven: thanks — deploy watch after merge.

maya: closing loop: rolling experiment on canary tomorrow with probe=true for 10% traffic. will report numbers. :rocket:
